master_predictions.verdict: On the six demands: (1) long life — 'according to natural Causes, he might live many yeers', nature being strong and he subject to few diseases; (2) Ireland would well agree with his constitution and he might get honour there; (3) his younger years would be the most pleasant of all his whole life; (4) past accidents recited (and confessed): molestation concerning lands or his wife's jointure/portion, great variance with his wife, and want of money for about six months before the question; (5)–(6) future: a treaty with some nobleman about the education of his child or children, support for about three years and three quarters, and then danger of losing his life, goods, lands and fortune, timed by the Moon wanting 7°22′ of the opposition of Mars.
reasoning_points: Finding the Ascendant not vitiated by Saturn (lord of the sixth) or Jupiter (lord of the eighth), the lord of the Ascendant (the Sun) in his exaltation, unimpeded and swift in the ninth, the Moon applying to a trine of Jupiter in mid-heaven, and the fortunate planets angular and more potent than the infortunes — long life
The Moon applying to Jupiter, the planet in the house of honours, and Jupiter placed in the sign which signifies Ireland — he was advised Ireland would agree with him and he might get honour there
The two fortunes in the tenth and the Sun and another in the ninth — his younger years the most pleasant; Mars in the eighth about the 24th–26th year of his age — crosses first beginning then

The Moon in the querent's second applying to Jupiter, lord of the fifth (children), and then to a trine of the lord of the eighth (the wife's substance) — a salary or treaty with a nobleman for the education of his children, settled out of the wife's fortune or jointure
The Moon separated from Mercury, lord of the second, by 6°21′ — want of money for about six moneths before the question (confessed)
The Moon wanting 7°22′ of the true opposition of Mars (Mars lord of the fourth, in the eighth) — after some three years and three quarters, danger to life, goods, lands and fortune
master_predictions.outcome: Recorded severally in the chapter: of long life, 'This hath hitherto proved true; he being yet alive this present, March 1646'; 'the Querent did go into Ireland, and there performed good service and obtained a notable Victory against the Rebels'; the children-education treaty 'he did settle before he went out of England'; after the timed period 'he was in severall actions both dangerous to his Person and Fortune', had honourable employment on his Majesty's part, 'yet is he now for ever, by Sentence of the Parliament, deprived of so much happinesse, as to end his dayes in England'. The past accidents (the wife's jointure variance, the six months' want of money) are marked 'This was confessed' / 'This was confessed also' in the text.

master_predictions.verdict: 'I judged the absent Brother was alive and had no manner of casualty happened unto him, but was in good health'; the querent would hear of him that very day (by the carriers of those countries); and he would come home within less than one week.
reasoning_points: Venus, significatrix of the brother (lady of the third), in no manner of way afflicted either by Mercury, lord of the eighth, or by Mars; the Moon's separation good (from a dexter trine of Jupiter) and her next application favourable — the absent alive and in health

Venus, significatrix of the quesited, and Saturn, lord of the Ascendant, applying to each other by a friendly trine which perfected that very day (five o'clock by the ephemeris, a little after four by the London meridian) — the querent should hear news of his brother very suddenly, that very day
Venus leaving a northern sign and entering a south sign — he was coming homewards towards his own house
The nature of the significators' sign and degrees in this question denoting a week — his return within less than one week
master_predictions.outcome: 'He hath since confidently affirmed, that about the very moment of time... a Carrier came casually to his house, and informed him his Brother was in health and living'; and 'he came home the Tuesday following, when the Moon came to [Venus]'.

master_predictions.verdict: 'You see here are eight testimonies of a Male Conception, or of Being with child of a Son; and but four of a Female; I therefore affirmed, that the Lady was impregnated of a Man child'; and, giving for every degree one week, 'that about fourteen weeks from the time of the Question, she should be delivered'.
reasoning_points: Plurality of masculine testimonies (eight) over feminine (four) among the proper significators — sign ascending, sign of the fifth, lord of the fifth, lord of the Ascendant, the Moon, the lord of the hour, and their signs and houses

The signs of the fifth are moveable, arguing a short time; but Saturn, lord of the fifth, being a ponderous planet of slow motion, and the Moon posited in the sign of the fifth, were much valued in the timing

The Moon's distance from the opposition of Saturn is 14°47′, and Mercury's distance from the body of Saturn 13°37′ — the two differing by only 1°10′, a degree was given for a week: about fourteen weeks
master_predictions.outcome: Of the sex: '(and so it proved)'; of the delivery: 'The truth is, she was delivered the eleventh of July following' (the 1852 edition adds that 13 weeks 4 days had elapsed).

master_predictions.verdict: 'I positively concluded, as to the parts of Body grieved, they were the Head, Brest, Heart and Stomack, and that there lodged in the Brest or Stomack some melanchollick Obstruction, the cause of all his disease and Misery'; the disease was permanent and not curable — medicines might only prolong his life, 'for the Moon in the fourth with Saturn argued sickness untill death'.
reasoning_points: Scorpio ascending, and the sixth house afflicted by a planet in his fall — from that house the part or member of the body afflicted was required
The sign of the sixth signifies the head; Saturn in it signifies the breast; the lord of the Ascendant signifies the heart

The lord of the Ascendant lately separated from a dexter square of Saturn, Saturn at that time in Cancer, which presents the breast and stomach — head, breast, heart and stomach grieved, with melancholy as principal cause and choler secondary
The Moon in the fourth in an earthly sign with Saturn, and all the angles fixed — sickness until death, the disease permanent
master_predictions.outcome: On speaking with the patient the symptoms were found exactly as judged: great pain and rumbling in his head, a very dry cough, great weakness and pain in his breast and at the heart, complexion as if inclined to the jaundice, a lingering consumption, red gravel and difficulty in making urine; 'He dyed the fourteenth of August following.'

master_predictions.verdict: The patient was 'wonderfully afflicted with the Spleen, with the Wind-chollick, and melancholly obstructions in the Bowels or small Guts, small Feavers... and as [the ascending sign] argued the sick was perplexed with distempers in his Head, slept unquietly, &c.'; and, 'I did not perceive by naturall causes, that he could live above ten or twelve dayes' — Lilly persuaded him to make his peace with God and settle his house in order.
reasoning_points: The Ascendant most afflicted by the corporal presence of a planet partly lord of the eighth; the sign of the sixth fixed and afflicted, its lord in a fixed, earthly, melancholly sign — the disease and member taken from the sixth and the Ascendant
The Sun, the temporal light (fons vitalis parentiae), in perfect opposition of Saturn, lord of the sixth, in fixed signs — death portended

The Moon neer the Dragon's Tail and afflicted by an infortune in the Ascendant, the house which signifies life; the Moon separating from the aspect of the lord of the Ascendant and transferring her virtue to the lord of the eighth
master_predictions.outcome: Of the disease: 'all which was true'; of the event: 'The sick dyed the 28th of July following' — twelve days after the figure of 16 July 1645.

master_predictions.verdict: 'I was confident the Match would suddenly be brought to passe by such a one as [the Moon] was, or represented by her, who did much interpose in the businesse' — the marriage would be effected, through the interposition of a person described by the Moon.
reasoning_points: Mercury, significatrix of the querent, retrograde under the Sun-beams — she was in great distresse and fear that the quesited would not have her
The quesited's significator in his exaltation and neer the sextile of Venus — an argument the man stood upon high termes, and had been tampering with another
Yet both significators were in a semi-sextile, and in good houses — 'there was some sparks of love betwixt them'

The Moon separating from a square of Jupiter, and carrying his light by a trine aspect to Mercury, lord of the Ascendant, he in an angle receiving willingly — the match suddenly brought to pass by a Moon-described interposer
master_predictions.outcome: Recorded within the judgment passage itself: that person 'at last, with a little difficulty, produced the Marriage to effect, to the content of both parties.'

master_predictions.verdict: 'He should not be hanged, but suffer a more noble kind of death, and that within the space of six or seven weeks, or thereabouts.'
reasoning_points: Being a man of the Church, his Ascendant is the cusp of the ninth house; Saturn, lord of the sign, in his fall, a long time retrograde, and posited in the twelfth of the figure — a violent spirit, involved in troubles, imprisoned

The Moon separating from Saturn and applying to the Sun neer the cusp of the eighth house; the Sun in a fiery sign applying to an opposition of Mars, the dispositor of the aged Bishop; Mars being in an airy sign and humane — not hanging, but a more noble death
The Moon wanting seven degrees of the body of Mars — the time, six or seven weeks
master_predictions.outcome: 'He was beheaded about the tenth of January following.'

master_predictions.verdict: The person of the Prince would be in no very great danger and 'we should not destroy his person'; but 'he should gain no honour by this War', should at last fall into the hatred and malice of many, and 'in the end should depart without either honour, love or friendship, but should not be killed'; 'Rupert should never prevaile against the valiant Essex'; and it should come to pass 'he should end at our disposing, and that we should at last have him in our own custody'.
reasoning_points: The Moon in a sign casting her sinister aspect to the cusp of the tenth, and Venus casting a dexter aspect to the same cusp — the person of the man in no very great danger, much honoured and respected, his person not destroyed

Neither of the luminaries in the tenth house or in perfect aspect with his significator; the lord of the tenth (the Sun) in his detriment in a fixed sign — no honour by the war, depraved fancy, obstinateness, departure without honour

Essex signified by Venus, lady of the opposite house, in reception with Saturn (she receives him in her house and term, and he her), Venus disposing of Rupert's significator — Rupert should never prevail against Essex, and should end at Parliament's disposing
master_predictions.outcome: Mixed, and recorded with Lilly's own correction: 'I positively affirmed, Rupert should never prevaile against the valiant Essex, &c., nor did he'; of the custody judgment, 'an errour in part I confess it was, yet... it was very neer truth, for in 1646 he was besieged in Oxford, and after surrender thereof... he was then at the mercy of the Parliament, and in their mercy: but they... let him depart... and so he escaped.'

master_predictions.verdict: (1) 'I did judge his Majesty should have ayde of Commanders out of Ireland... that they should harm us', but they would produce much scandall to his Majesty, and though he was likely to augment his forces for some certain time, 'it should not continue very long'. (2) The Queen would move forwards with her army with intention to meet his Majesty, 'about three or four moneths from the time of the Figure'; 'I judged that she would not prosper but decline', and would be crossed at or neer the aspect of the 11th of April, losing some forces about Nottingham.
reasoning_points: The Moon, his Majesty's significator, in Cancer in the tenth, in her own house, increasing in light, elevated and void of infelicity — his Majesty at the time in an able condition

The Sun, lord of the eleventh (assistance or aid), in the seventh in his exaltation, in direct opposition to the Ascendant which represented the Parliament — Irish aid that should harm them; but the Sun beholding the cusp of the tenth with a sinister square — Lilly in the end less feared them, and judged they should produce much scandall to his Majesty; and neither the Sun nor the Moon being fixed, the augmentation of his forces should not continue very long

Her Majesty's significatrix Saturn, lord of the fourth, removing out of one sign into another — she would move forwards with her army; the Moon wanting three or four degrees of Saturn's trine — the meeting in three or four months
Saturn going into Aries, his fall, and good fortune separated from him — she would not prosper but decline; Mars hastening to an opposition of Saturn — crossed about the 11th of April
master_predictions.outcome: 'The truth is, he had Irish Forces came over, which much hardned the hearts of the English against him, but time cut them off... at the Siege of Nantwich, by valiant Fairfax'; 'The truth is, she met him about the 14. of July 1443 [sic — misprint for 1643] in Warwick-shire'; and at the April aspect, 'about Nottingham she lost some Forces'.

master_predictions.verdict: 'In the end he should obtain the Office', 'with some difficulty... notwithstanding the opposition the pretended Friend did make'; and the solar man he employed as a friend 'was false, and did rather envy then affect him'.
reasoning_points: The Moon placed in the tenth, which is the house of the thing looked after, viz. preferment — one argument the querent should have it
The Moon applying to a trine of Saturn, who hath exaltation in the Ascendant, receives Venus and is received of her again; Saturn also lord of the fourth — in the end he should obtain the office
The Sun in the seventh house in opposition to the Ascendant and with the Dragon's Tail, he being lord of the eleventh — he employed as a friend a solar man who was false
The Moon separating from a square of Mercury — he had delivered many petitions about it, but hitherto without success
master_predictions.outcome: 'and so it came to passe within lesse three weekes [1647 OCR reading; the 1852 edition reads 'within three weeks'], and he then discovered that his Friend was false, who had a great scar in his Face, was not of bright or yellow Hair, but of a blackish, dark colour'.

master_predictions.verdict: 'I judged the Querent should have his Goods or Horse quickly and unexpectedly, within a day or two from the time of the Question asked'; the thief could not keep him; the horse had gone full west, but because his significator was retrograde, 'I judged the Horse would not proceed far, but return again to his proper owner'.
reasoning_points: The lord of the twelfth (the horse) retrograde, by his retrograde motion applying to the lord of the querent's house of substance, and the Moon locally in the second — recovery quickly and unexpectedly
The seventh house afflicted — the thief could not keep him
The sign of the twelfth west, the sign wherein its lord was west, and the lord of the fourth in a west sign — the horse was gone full west
His significator retrograde — he would not proceed far, but return again; and two retrograde planets upon the cusp of the second usually shew quick and unexpected recovery
master_predictions.outcome: 'and indeed the Horse did come home three dayes after, and had been full West. However, I judged the Horse would have been at home a day sooner' — recovery and direction as judged, timing one day later than judged; the horse came home Wednesday or Thursday the 13th or 14th of January, 'and it was very true' of those who rode him away.

master_predictions.verdict: 'I positively affirmed he was not bewitched'; the disease was occult, and 'lay in the Reines and Secrets, and occasioned by too much Venereal sports' — 'a Female Disease, closely obtained', though 'I did not say it was a perfect Lues Venerea'; he was itchy, and the disease was all over his body, in his joynts, and in his blood, that being corrupted; Lilly directed them again to advise with the doctors, and civilly to acquaint them that the disease was occult.
reasoning_points: Neither the lord of the twelfth afflicting the lord of the Ascendant, nor the Ascendant itself or the Moon so afflicted — there is no strong witchcraft
The Moon going to an opposition of Saturn, both planets in the sixth and twelfth houses, gave suspicion of witchcraft (and the failure of physic gave the querents reason for it), but did not prove it

Saturn on the cusp of the sixth and the lady of his sign in the twelfth — an occult, secret disease, and venereal; the Moon after her opposition of Saturn applying to the lord of the Ascendant — return to the doctors
master_predictions.outcome: 'This advice was followed, the course of Physick altered, and the afflicted party in or about three weeks perfectly recovered.'

master_predictions.verdict: The prisoner would go eastward, or full east; he was not yet out of town, but lay obscurely for a while, about a night, then would go away; 'I confidently affirmed, he should be recovered again, and taken by some man of authority'; and the querent should have news of the prisoner by letter, or by some young man, within six or seven days.
reasoning_points: The sign of the twelfth, the sign wherein Jupiter (the prisoner's significator) is, the quarter of heaven, and the sign wherein the Moon is — all considered, they signified unanimously that the prisoner would go eastward
The nearness of the Moon to the Ascendant shewed he was not yet out of town; Jupiter in the eighth house — he lay obscurely for a while, viz. a night, but then would go away
The Moon separating from a trine of Jupiter and applying to an opposition of the Sun, both in angles — the fugitive or prisoner is again taken, by authority
Jupiter and Mercury in aspect, Mercury in his own house and applying to Jupiter — news by letter or by some young man within six or seven days
master_predictions.outcome: Eastward: '(and so he did)'; the obscure night: '(so he did)'; 'The truth is, the Friday after, he had a Letter where he was, and the Sunday after apprehended him again by authority.'

master_predictions.verdict: She should neither care to make friends to his Majesty or any else for delivery of her husband, 'for I was assured he either was, or would within three dayes be discharged of his imprisonment, by means of a Solar man, a Commander, who would release him and furnish him with what was convenient for his necessity'.
reasoning_points: Jupiter, lord of the seventh (the lady's husband), in Cancer retrograde but in his exaltation, and lately, or the day before, in a trine with the Sun
The Moon applying to a sextile of Saturn retrograde, then to a trine of Jupiter, with a most forcible reception — short imprisonment and discharge
Jupiter exalted and in a perfect trine of the Sun, who is lord of the fourth — the end of the matter a release by a solar man, a commander
master_predictions.outcome: 'The very truth is, he was released, and the Garrison where he was prisoner taken the same day before the Question was asked, by an honest Parliament-Colonel, who plentifully relieved him with Money, and all convenient necessaries.'

master_predictions.verdict: The Earl 'should have slender successe and much losse by this his present March'; he would be 'betrayed in his Counsels'; 'I onely gave this Judgment, that his Excellency must expect no successe from this imployment, that he would have no honour by the Journey, that he would be extreamly crossed... and be in danger to lose all'.
reasoning_points: The Moon separating from a trine of Saturn and applying to a square of Mars, lord of his substance, assistants, friends and journeys — slender success and much loss
The Dragon's Tail in the Ascendant — he would be betrayed in his counsels

Saturn, lord of the Ascendant, peregrine and in his fall in the second, and the Moon in her detriment, and the Part of Fortune disposed by Mercury, lord of the seventh, a significator of his enemies — no honour, extreme crossing, danger to lose all
master_predictions.outcome: 'The issue is this (for I write to Posterity): he prospered in the beginning, and I was daily by men of good quality and of authority jeered at, and derided for my former prediction... But behold, the eighth of September following came sad news, that the second of September this worthy man had surrendered all his Ammunition to his Majesty, having onely Quarter for his Souldiers' — the Lostwithiel surrender, 2 September 1644.
